violations_found.violations:
- Organizational Constraint violated: The narrative states the EU runs three measures (two large, one small) and also names a priority, implying four active measures or designations. However, Constitutional Constraint 5 limits the EU to at most one new measure per turn and at most one named priority. While the notepad shows the Emergency Sovereignty Reinforcement Directive as a new measure (charge −2), the portfolio charge in the notepad includes four items (three ongoing measures and a priority), which is permissible only if they were introduced over multiple turns. The narrative, however, introduces the Emergency Sovereignty Reinforcement Directive *in this turn* while also maintaining two other large measures and a priority—this would require introducing more than one new measure or exceeding the one-priority limit unless all were previously established. The notepad does not clearly indicate that only one new measure (the Directive) was introduced this turn, and the phrasing "the EU runs three measures" plus a priority suggests all are active simultaneously without clarifying their turn-by-turn introduction. This violates Constraint 5: "At most one new measure per turn, and at most one named priority."
- Economic Constraint violated: The new measure, Emergency Sovereignty Reinforcement Directive, is described as a high-cost policy (given its scope across critical sectors and mandated technical migration) and is assigned a portfolio charge of −2, which under standard interpretation corresponds to a small or medium cost. However, more critically, the directive is introduced and expected to take effect by "turn 14", implying full implementation within one turn. Constitutional Constraint 6 requires a minimum of two full turns for high-cost measures to be implemented. Even if effect grows gradually, the narrative implies operational mandates (migration or fallback activation) will be required by the next turn, violating the minimum time lag for high-cost measures.
